newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel in uproar over alleged Netanyahu corruption.
newsitem.headline: Israel in uproar over alleged Netanyahu corruption.

text.p: Israeli jurists and opposition lawmakers called on Thursday for an inquiry into a media allegation of criminal corruption in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.
All those named in the Israel Television report, including Netanyahu, denied any wrongdoing.

The state television said on Wednesday that Netanyahu agreed to appoint an attorney general who was being pushed by a key coalition party leader, Aryeh Deri of the Shas party who is embroiled in a corruption trial.

The report said Deri had won from the proposed attorney general Roni Bar-On -- a Jerusalem attorney and activist in Netanyahu's Likud party -- a promise of a plea bargain that would let him continue his political career.

The television alleged Deri, on trial since 1993, threatened to withdraw Shas' support for Netanyahu's deal with the PLO on Israeli West Bank troop redeployments if Bar-On was not appointed attorney general.

Netanyahu appointed Bar-On this month in a move that drew public protests from Israel's legal establishment. Bar-On resigned within 12 hours under withering criticism he was a legal lightweight appointed to kowtow to Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing and religious parties.
Shas last week helped Netanyahu crush a rightist cabinet rebellion on the accord to hand over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule.
"I had no deal with anyone," Bar-On was quoted as telling Israel radio.
"Lies and falsehoods," Deri's personal assistant Yehuda Avidan said.
Reuters was unable to contact Bar-On or Deri for comment.
"Absolute nonsense," Netanyahu told Israel television about the allegations.
But Yossi Sarid, leader of the left-wing Meretz party, turned to police investigators and acting Attorney General Edna Arbel to check the allegations.
"We are talking about the largest corruption scandal in the history of the state if the story is correct," Sarid told Israel radio.
"Routine denials and a return to business as usual will not suffice," Sarid said, adding that Netanyahu himself must be investigated.
Labour party lawmakers, jurists and Israel's Movement for Quality Government also called for state and police inquiries.
"If this is correct...it is an attempt by criminals or apparent criminals to control the criminal justice system," legal analyst Moshe Negbi told army radio.
Israel television reporter Ayala Hasson, who broke the story, insisted her information was water-tight but declined to reveal her sources.
"We wouldn't raise information like this if we weren't convinced from all directions," she said.

Justice Minister Tsahi Hanegbi, who presented Bar-On's appointment to the cabinet, told Israel radio that Hasson should disclose her sources: "It seems to me there is a lot of speculation from crumbs of information."
Hanegbi, who was once Bar-On's clerk, took the blame for the failed appointment but the television said he was only a scapegoat.
